questions.prompt: Which OSI model layer is responsible for end-to-end communication, flow control, and error recovery using TCP and UDP?
questions.explanation: The Transport Layer (Layer 4) manages end-to-end transport services, packet segmentation, reliability (TCP), or connectionless speed (UDP).

questions.prompt: What protocol is used by network devices to automatically assign IP addresses to client systems?
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and DNS servers to host devices.

questions.definition: The hierarchical, decentralized naming system that translates human-readable domain names (e.g. google.com) into numeric IP addresses (e.g. 142.250.190.46).
questions.explanation: Often referred to as the 'Phonebook of the Internet'.

questions.prompt: Match standard network protocols to their default TCP/UDP port numbers:
questions.explanation: Standard well-known ports defined by IANA for core Internet communication protocols.

questions.prompt: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits in length, represented as eight groups of four hexadecimal digits.
questions.explanation: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses (compared to IPv4's 32-bit addresses), vastly expanding available unique IP addresses across the globe.

questions.prompt: Arrange the standard 3-Way TCP Handshake connection packets in proper sequence:
items: Client replies with ACK (Acknowledge) to establish connection
questions.explanation: The classic TCP 3-way handshake follows SYN -> SYN-ACK -> ACK to establish a reliable end-to-end transmission session.
